about: Before rebuilding a about page for an agency or studio, read Portfolio About: the composition and the specification behind it are both here. Colour is limited to black #0C0C0C underneath and white #D7E2EA for the type, set in Kanit. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS — one page, no plugin, no build tooling between you and the design. Motion is 200ms transitions, kept quiet enough that the copy still leads. Start from the captured brief, then edit the about page rather than rebuilding it from scratch.

layout.title: The brief names the steps
layout.body: Type and spacing are drawn from one list here: 160px spacing steps and 200ms transitions. There is no invented intermediate value between the named ones; the measurement list is the whole system.

layout.title: Badge above the fold
layout.body: One badge, one message: the pill sits above the headline in Kanit at the smallest step, and nothing else competes for that slot. The pill sits at the smallest step in the brief, so it reads as a label rather than as a second title.

layout.title: Copy first, decoration second
layout.body: The about page is built so the copy lands before anything else: the type carries the hierarchy, the 640x468 frame holds the composition, and the supporting values stay quiet. The page is one composition at 640x468, which is why it holds together when the copy changes. The brief is the specification.

layout.title: Numbers carried into the build
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (160px spacing steps and 200ms transitions), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: The whole animation budget
motion.body: Every state change in the specification has a duration attached: transitions settle around 200ms. Nothing is left at the browser default, which is why the page feels authored rather than animated. One value is reused across the controls, so their timing cannot drift apart.

motion.title: Reveals tied to movement
motion.body: The effect sits on top of a finished layout rather than generating it, so the page is readable with a sticky element holds position while the content moves under it disabled. Reduced motion drops the effect without changing the composition's final state. The reference was captured at 640x468.

notes: Transitions are specified at 200ms, which is the value to keep when the palette changes. The reference was captured at 640x468, and every value quoted on this page comes from the same brief.
The timing budget is state feedback rather than page choreography (200ms), so a slower rebuild reads as a different design.

customize: Load your own face beside Kanit and compare the headline at full width before committing to the swap.
Read the brief value by value against the 640x468 capture before you edit anything; the numbers are the part that is easiest to lose.
Hold the 640x468 frame when you swap the content; the composition was solved against that ratio and a wider export pushes the type off.
Swap Kanit for a face with the same x-height and cap height, then re-measure the headline block.

editorial.title: Making the about page yours
editorial.body: When you drop your own media in, keep the crop and the layer order. The media is a still at 640x468. That placement is what keeps the copy legible. If a new element does not help explain the offer or the next action, it belongs below the fold.

editorial.title: How Portfolio About sequences the first read
editorial.body: Set your own copy into this about page and the sequence still holds, because the elements are not interchangeable: the announcement badge, the stats row and the feature list each carry one job. A agency reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What holds up for Agencies & Studios
editorial.body: 5,431 characters of brief produce one screen with no filler. The values in it are explicit (160px spacing steps and 200ms transitions), which is why the composition still reads when the words change. Portfolio About states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.question: Is the Portfolio About prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 5,431 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How is this Portfolio About entry organised?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 5,431-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Portfolio About was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

audience: If the reference is only a starting point, designers can keep a 640x468 frame and rebuild the rest of the about page.
Product teams writing their own About page copy who need every line to keep the length the display type was sized for.
